text:
Diego Alvarez: hey all — first week on Monday, tiny laundry list: 1) I9m converting from a Japan-based contractor to US FT. My offer says benefits start on start date but my previous insurer says I have a 30-day waiting period for outpatient until carrier confirms. Does Redwood backdate or coordinate? 2) I received a $2,000 one-time relocation stipend paid to my JP account in JPY; payroll flagged bank country mismatch. Will that be grossed on my first US paycheck or treated as a separate AP payment? 3) I paid a property forwarding company in JPY — receipt attached (I will upload) 5,000 JPY. Do you need the original receipt + bank statement? 4) My visa stamping appointment is the day before the company holiday — if I9m delayed, will benefits effective date move?

Nita (People Ops): welcome Diego! :wave: Quick answers: (1) We rely on the carrier for effective coverage. Typically the plan effective date is your FT start date in Workday. If the carrier enforces a 30-day internal waiting window we escalate to Benefits vendor to request an exception when it's pre-existing coverage switching. Please DM me your prior insurer details and policy number.

Nita (People Ops): (2) Relocation stipend: since it was paid to your JP account before conversion we treat pre-start gross payments per the offer as taxable income; however we reconcile on payroll. If the stipend was explicitly labeled "relocation allowance" we may offset. Payroll will confirm classification (gross vs reimbursement).

Carlos (Payroll): tagging in. For cross-border bank issues: if a payment is in JPY to a JP bank and your US bank details later don't match, we typically do one of: a) gross it on first US payroll (USD conversion), or b) issue via AP wire if it's reimbursement. For your case, since company already issued to your JP account, please upload the payment proof and let us know whether you want us to net anything out. We need the original JP bank advice + proof of payment.

Carlos (Payroll): Diego — receipts: yes attach the original vendor invoice + screenshot of the JP bank transfer (SWIFT advice or bank statement showing debit). For FX conversion we use payroll9s FX snapshot on the payroll run date. Also send us the last 4 of the JP account for verification if you9re comfortable.

Diego Alvarez: thanks. I uploaded the forwarding receipt and bank SWIFT advice to the expense portal. Also DMd last 4 of JP acct. Regarding the stipend, the vendor label is "relocation allowance" and was wired by company before my conversion — I9m not sure if that changes treatment.

Benefits Bot: :information_source: Note: Prior coverage coordination requires policy number and effective/from-to dates. Upload prior insurer PDF to this thread or DM Nita.

Nita (People Ops): if the company wired pre-conversion, that is typically treated as a grossed pre-start payment. We can classify as a relocation taxable stipend on payroll. I9ll confirm with Legal if there are any cross-border withholding nuances.

Diego Alvarez: last Q 5 about visa/holiday timing: start date in Workday is still the official effective date even if visa stamping delays your physical arrival. If visa delay prevents completion of I-9 or benefits enrollment by payroll cutoff, Payroll will provision with pending flags and benefits vendor will hold until docs are complete. That can delay card activation but not retroactively change the start date.

Carlos (Payroll): final note on timeline: once we have receipts and SWIFT advice, AP can net any overpayment or process reimbursement. Expect to see the reconciliation on your first paycheck or an AP wire within 7-10 business days after approval. If your US direct deposit fails due to country mismatch we will issue a check which can be slower.

Diego Alvarez: perfect, thanks team. I9ll upload the old insurer PDF and keep an eye on the payroll notes. Appreciate the quick responses!
